definition: Fixing the criterion a result must meet before the result is measured, so that a threshold cannot be chosen after seeing the data. Both sources are from the same research programme and both use it in the way that costs them something. The identifiability work reports two pre-registered criteria that fail their controls: an invariance-gap criterion met in 49 percent of 75 cells against a registered 80 percent, because the sign of the effect tracks the feature-selection rule, and a universality criterion that separates two seed replicas of one architecture and therefore, in its stated form, is not a universality criterion. Both are reported because both bound what may be claimed. The cross-layer ablation work applies it to mechanism selection, reporting three rejected candidate mechanisms because they had been pre-registered -- which the archive's reading notes cuts both ways, since it also means the retained mechanism was selected for cleanliness. Neither source treats pre-registration as a subject; between them they demonstrate its only real function, which is to make a negative result reportable rather than discardable.

evidence.note: Extends a single-block interaction theorem to ablated subsets spanning many layers, isolates the cross-layer remainder as an exact double integral rather than bounding it, supplies the one missing closed-form ingredient (a local attention Jacobian bound, verified without a violation on a real 1.5B model), and tests the whole picture on an emergent circuit nobody designed for it — reporting the mixed outcome as mixed.
evidence.title: Cross-Layer Interaction under Weight-Space Ablation: A Closed-Form Attention Jacobian Bound and a Test on a Real Pretrained Model

evidence.note: Treats a transformer forward pass as a controlled dynamical system with depth as time, lifts it with the Koopman operator to get a finite linear realisation whose spectrum is coordinate-free, proves that spectrum is recoverable from finite calibration data at the parametric rate, and then proves that the identifiable object and the human-legible object cannot be the same object.
evidence.title: Intrinsic Structure: Spectral Identifiability for Mechanistic Interpretability

evidence.note: Points out that the group-relative policy gradient is a second-order U-statistic over pairs of rollouts rather than a sum of independent per-rollout contributions, and reallocates rollout compute accordingly -- treating prefixes as vertices and pair-gradient terms as edges, then correcting the resulting selection bias by inverse joint-inclusion weighting.
evidence.title: PAIR: Pairwise-Aware Inclusion Reweighting for Adaptive Rollout Allocation in RLVR

evidence.note: Measures, under a pre-registered confirmatory design, how often majority-vote self-consistency lowers per-problem accuracy on a hard science benchmark, and shows that two cheap verifier-free gates recover essentially none of the headroom a per-problem oracle marks out.
evidence.title: When Self-Consistency Backfires: Majority Vote Hurts the Majority of Hard Science Problems for Small LLMs

name: pre-registration
